messages.subject: Spatial Mark-Resight in oSCR?
messages.body_plain:
Hey gang,

Is there a way to analyze spatial mark-resight data using oSCR? More specifically, adding encounters of unmarked individuals to your EDF.

Just looking for something similar to the addSightings() function from the secr package, but since I have telemetry data to integrate, as well, I thought using the oSCR package might be the better option.

Thanks very much.
Wes

We don’t have that functionality in oSCR. You might want to contact Ben Augustine about his SPIM work, he could recommend an approach whether using his R package or JAGS/Nimble.

I will say that adding the unknown ID encounters is not very valuable unless your SCR data are very sparse. Depends on context though...

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for getting back to me, Dan.

Reaching out to Ben would be a good idea, thanks for the recommendation. I know he has worked on a gSMR study before that was very similar to what I'm trying to accomplish. I just wonder how well I would be able to follow some of Ben's complex coding!

We are working with a small study area and currently have a relatively large proportion of the population 'marked' with GPS collars, so ignoring the unmarked encounters and running things through oSCR might still be worthwhile. One reason I thought incorporating unmarked detections would help our density/abundance estimates is because there is a lot of landscape heterogeneity here that influences density, and thus need our estimates (and state-space) to reflect this. I figured that incorporating the unmarked detections would be a straightforward way of addressing this, but perhaps using a SCR-RSF model in oSCR would alleviate some of these concerns. I really just need to show how some covariates like ruggedness and elevation influence density, so the RSF may be the ticket to accomplishing that.

Thanks,
Wes

I'm wondering if others have dealt with this successfully or if this error could be for a different reason than the starting values?

Jeff

On Wednesday, September 2, 2020 at 7:54:57 AM UTC-4 danl...@gmail.com wrote:
> Reposting my response:
>
> Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).
>
> You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.
>
> I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.
>
> The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:
>
> #set specific starting values:
> specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
> #have at it
> oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)
>
> Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.
>
> So, in short:
>
> 1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
> 2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
> 3) play with starting values for sigma
>
> Let me know how that goes!
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeff,

We are about to publish a new method for integrating telemetry data into SCR which we hope to add to oSCR sometime soon. Not soon enough for you, but if you are interested in seeing the preprint, or more specifically the code for fitting the model, let me know.

A feature of the approach is that it estimates separately a 'movement' sigma and an SCR sigma. In discussions with Dan, we wondered whether assuming they are the same value might be part of the issue folks are having.

Let me know.

Chris

> On Wednesday, September 2, 2020 at 7:54:57 AM UTC-4 danl...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Reposting my response:
> >
> > Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).
> >
> > You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.
> >
> > I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.
> >
> > The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:
> >
> > #set specific starting values:
> > specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
> > #have at it
> > oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)
> >
> > Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.
> >
> > So, in short:
> >
> > 1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
> > 2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
> > 3) play with starting values for sigma
> >
> > Let me know how that goes!

Thanks Chris. If you can share the code and preprint that would be great.

Jeff

On Wed, May 19, 2021 at 12:48 PM Chris Sutherland <chris...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Jeff,
>
> We are about to publish a new method for integrating telemetry data into SCR which we hope to add to oSCR sometime soon. Not soon enough for you, but if you are interested in seeing the preprint, or more specifically the code for fitting the model, let me know.
>
> A feature of the approach is that it estimates separately a 'movement' sigma and an SCR sigma. In discussions with Dan, we wondered whether assuming they are the same value might be part of the issue folks are having.
>
> Let me know.
>
> Chris
>
> On Wed, 19 May 2021, 15:28 jthomps...@gmail.com, <jthomps...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hello. I have a near identical situation as this post (actually my telemetry data are dependent but I am ignoring that for now), however, despite all of Dan's suggestions I am still getting the same error. I'm wondering if others have dealt with this successfully or if this error could be for a different reason than the starting values?
> >
> > Jeff
> >
> > On Wednesday, September 2, 2020 at 7:54:57 AM UTC-4 danl...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > Reposting my response:
> > >
> > > Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).
> > >
> > > You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.
> > >
> > > I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.
> > >
> > > The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:
> > >
> > > #set specific starting values:
> > > specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
> > > #have at it
> > > oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)
> > >
> > > Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.
> > >
> > > So, in short:
> > >
> > > 1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
> > > 2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
> > > 3) play with starting values for sigma
> > >
> > > Let me know how that goes!
> > >
> > > On Tue, Sep 1, 2020 at 5:08 PM Katherine Kurth <kathy...@gmail.com> wrote:
